reason: execute() always logs at least one 'attempt started' before 'operation finished' (for-loop body runs before finish).
the loop breaks after 'operation succeeded'; a further 'attempt started' can only follow 'temporary failure, retrying'.
'temporary failure, retrying' is followed by `continue`: the next log must be a new 'attempt started', not 'operation succeeded'.
'attempt started' is logged only inside execute(), which always logs 'operation started' first.
an execution that logged 'temporary failure, retrying' must continue with a new attempt or 'retry budget exhausted'; the trace has no terminal.
'operation started' is logged exactly once per execute() call; the loop never returns to the method entry.
